title: Why Slot Machines Hook People
objective: After this level you can explain reinforcement schedules and why unpredictable rewards keep a behavior going longest.
summary: Rewards can come every time or only sometimes, by count or by time. Unpredictable variable ratio rewards, used in gambling, are the hardest to extinguish.

cards.headline: A slot machine pays after an unpredictable number of pulls. That's the trap.
cards.body: You'd think unpredictable rewards would make people give up sooner. The research on reward timing says the opposite. It comes down to the timing of rewards, known as reinforcement schedules.

cards.headline: Every time, or only sometimes
cards.body: Reward a behavior every single time and you're using continuous reinforcement. Reward it only some of the time and it's partial, or intermittent, reinforcement. Partial schedules come in four kinds, sorted by two questions. Is the reward based on how many responses you make (ratio) or on how much time has passed (interval)? And is that number fixed or variable?

items.label: Ratio: counts your responses
points: Fixed: reward after a predictable number
Variable: reward after an unpredictable number

cards.headline: Why the slot machine wins
cards.body: Most gambling runs on a variable ratio schedule: the next pull might pay, or the one after that, or much later. Each win adds money right after a pull, which is positive reinforcement, delivered unpredictably. Of the four schedules, variable ratio gets the most responding and is the most resistant to extinction; fixed interval is the easiest to extinguish. More broadly, behavior rewarded only now and then lasts longer once rewards stop than behavior rewarded every time, an effect long seen as central to why people keep gambling without winning.

cards.headline: Why Slot Machines Hook People
learned: Continuous: reward every time; partial: only sometimes
Ratio counts responses; interval counts time
Variable ratio is the hardest to extinguish
Most gambling pays on a variable ratio schedule

questions.prompt: Of the reinforcement schedules, the _____ schedule is the most resistant to extinction.

options.label: fixed interval
options.rationale: Fixed interval is the easiest to extinguish.

options.label: fixed ratio
options.rationale: Predictable counts don't hold on as long.

options.label: variable interval
options.rationale: Unpredictable timing helps, but it isn't the strongest.

questions.explanation: Variable ratio schedules are the most productive and the most resistant to extinction.

questions.prompt: Match each kind of reinforcement with its description.
questions.explanation: Continuous reinforcement rewards a behavior every single time. Variable ratio is the most resistant to extinction, and fixed interval is the easiest to extinguish.

questions.prompt: A slot machine win adds money right after a pull. Which of the four kinds of consequences is that?

options.label: Positive punishment
options.rationale: Punishment makes a behavior less likely.

questions.explanation: Adding something desirable to increase a behavior is positive reinforcement.
